_comment: Curated A9 test point expectations, hand-authored from the 1996 Series II
service manual: §5-10 and §5-11 (page 5-56 to 5-57) for the bench procedure,
§5-2 for the 3300-series fault codes, and §2-173 to §2-185 for what each node
is. Figure 7-9 sheets 1-4 were read alongside to confirm which net each test
point actually sits on, and the signal names and sheet zones below are
transcribed from the TEST POINT INFORMATION box at zone D1 of sheet 1, which
prints them as 'TP1 = OHMS OUT HI (PG1 C7)' -- page 1, zone C7.
A9 has no supply table in Chapter 2 and no supply rail of its own that the
manual tabulates. It runs on +/-17 S, S COM, +5 RLH, RLH COM, +5 LH, LH COM
and -5 LH delivered through P312 by A17 and A19, and makes exactly one pair
of its own -- the +/-8A floating supply that powers the two-wire compensation
amplifiers -- whose only published expectation is §5-11 step 1. Everything
here was therefore read out of the manual text directly. What that means:
* TP3 and TP4 do not exist. The sheet 1 legend prints both as 'NOT USED',
and Table 6-10's jumper row is 'TP1,TP2,TP5-20' -- eighteen wire loops,
numbered 1, 2 and 5 through 20. They are absent here rather than carried
as empty entries.
* Seven of the eighteen have no published level at all. TP1, TP6, TP7,
TP10, TP12, TP17 and TP19 are either returns or the low lead of somebody
else's measurement, and TP11, TP15 are nodes the manual never tabulates.
Each carries isReturn or noPublishedValue rather than a guess.
* The fault-code bands are printed as '±3% ±15 mV', a per-cent term plus a
floor. The schema takes one number, so each entry carries the arithmetic
sum as an absolute tolerance and the note shows the working. That is the
band the manual stands behind, not a tightening or a loosening of it.
* TP16 and TP18 are the only two values in this file marked inferred. §5-11
step 2 gives them as prose -- 'should be around 5.0V' and 'about -10V' --
with no tolerance at all, and says outright that the criterion is the
ratio: TP16 must be twice TP18's reading and of opposite polarity
(gain = -2). The +/-20 % written below is this dataset's, wide enough not
to fail a working board on the manual's own vagueness. Judge the ratio.
* §5-10 step 2 is a four-terminal resistance measurement across TP1/TP2
with the sense leads on TP5/TP6, not a voltage at any one point, so it
lives in probePoints as three resistance checks rather than being spread
across four test points that would each carry a quarter of it.
Commons are not interchangeable on this board and the procedures use three.
§5-11 step 1 is referenced to TP7 (ACOM), which is the floating common of the
two-wire compensation supply and is not tied to S COM; the source and diff-amp
checks are referenced to TP12 (SCOM) and TP10 (RCOM/SCOM); and the digital
section runs on +5 RLH to RLH COM and +5 LH to LH COM, neither of which has a
test point at all.

testpoints.note: The high side of the selected resistance as it leaves A9 for the output bus, at P311 pins 12A/12C. No single-ended level is published for it: it is used twice as a connection rather than as a reading. §5-10 step 2 puts the four-terminal ohmmeter's IN HI here, and fault code 3313 uses it as the DMM's *low* lead while the hi lead sits on TP2. Relays K4 and K5 connect the 1 ohm and 1.9 ohm values to this line and K7/K8 select the short.

testpoints.condition: During diagnostic 3313: the 2/5/10 V source set to 10 V across the 20 kohm made from Z5's 10 kohm in series with A10's 10 kohm string.
testpoints.note: Published as 5 V ±3 % ±15 mV, which is ±0.150 V + 0.015 V = ±0.165 V. Note the polarity the manual asks for: DMM hi on TP2 and low on TP1, which is the reverse of what the names suggest. The verdict is branched -- greater than 5 V blames A10, less than or equal to 5 V blames A9 -- so record the sign, not just the magnitude. Outside the 3313 test this point is simply the low side of the resistance bus (P311 pins 9A/9C), where §5-10 step 2 puts the ohmmeter's IN LO. Relays K6 and K30 connect the 1 ohm and 1.9 ohm values to it, and K24 connects it on to OUT LO.

testpoints.condition: During diagnostic 3325: A7 sourcing 0.13 mA through A10's 10 kohm string via INT OUT HI.
testpoints.note: Published as 1.3 V ±3 % ±15 mV, which is ±0.039 V + 0.015 V = ±0.054 V. The verdict branches the other way from 3313's: out of tolerance blames the Ohms Main assembly (A10), in tolerance blames A9. Outside that test this is the sense high line arriving at P311 pins 11A/11C, where §5-10 step 2 puts the ohmmeter's SENSE HI; K29 routes it to U7's -input during two-wire compensation.

Sense low, at P311 pins 8A/8C. Nothing is published for it on its own; it is the low lead for fault code 3325's 1.3 V reading at TP5, the ohmmeter's SENSE LO in §5-10 step 2, and the DMM's low lead for the 1 kohm-in-Z2 measurement of §5-11 step 2. The low-side cancelling current from U9 reaches the calibration resistor through K28A on this line.

The common of the floating supply that powers U7 and U8, and the point the ohmmeter's own current enters A9 at. It is NOT S COM: the two-wire compensation supply floats on it, which is the whole point of the circuit. §5-11 step 1 is referenced here and nowhere else. Note that the sheet 1 legend prints this as ACOM; the curated study document in ../MD/ calls it RCOM, which is a different net on this board and a different common.

testpoints.condition: Calibrator set to 100 ohm, operate, two-wire comp ON.
testpoints.note: Positive half of the floating supply for the compensation amplifiers, regulated by 8.2 V zener VR1 off the rectified T1 secondary and filtered by R43, L3 and C24. Absent PB7 turning Q6 and Q5 on, +17 S never reaches U6 and this rail is simply dead -- so a zero here with the two-wire comp switched off is correct. If both rails are wrong, §5-11 step 1 has you scope U6 pin 16 with the common on pin 13 before touching anything.

testpoints.condition: Calibrator set to 100 ohm, operate, two-wire comp ON.
testpoints.note: Negative half of the same floating supply, regulated by 8.2 V zener VR2 and filtered by R44, L4 and C25. The manual prints the expectation as '-8.2V ±5%' -- the sign is stated here, unlike the unsigned magnitudes in the Chapter 2 supply tables.

The point where R COM (P311 pins 23A/23C) and S COM are brought together on sheet 1, through K27. It is the low lead for fault code 3315's 0.2 V check at TP20. Not the same common as TP7: the two-wire compensation supply floats relative to this.

The tap of the Z1 divider that sets the 2/5/10 V source, ahead of buffer U1 and pass transistor Q1. §2-181 describes what the divider does -- the buffered 13 V reference from A11 arrives through K9, and Q2/Q3 driven by PB4/PB5 parallel Z1's 11.535 kohm and 3.846 kohm sections with its 50 kohm to drop the output to 2 V -- but publishes no level at this node, and no fault code names it. The published check on this circuit is at TP13. Useful for separating a bad divider from a bad buffer: if TP13 is wrong and TP11 tracks the commanded level, look at U1 and Q1.

S COM as it arrives on P312 pins 1A/1C, and the ground plane reference for the 2/5/10 V source and the differential amplifier -- sheet 2 marks both blocks 'GROUND PLANE = SCOM'. The low lead for fault code 3304's 10 V check at TP13.

Output of the 2/5/10 V source -- the current source behind every resistance ratio measurement the instrument makes. Three commanded levels, each with its own diagnostic; only the 10 V case names TP13 and TP12 outright, and the 5 V and 2 V bands are the same codes' published tolerances applied at the same point, which is why they are marked inferred. The note printed against all three codes matters: if extender cards are available, verify that 10V SENSE LO is tied to SCOM, a connection made by relays on both Ohms assemblies. For 3304 the manual also branches on the result -- out of tolerance means the source itself, in tolerance means the diagnostic circuit (U21 and the Z3/Z4 dividers) instead.

states.label: Source commanded to 10 V
states.source: §5-2 fault code 3304 (DMM hi TP13, low TP12)

states.label: Source commanded to 5 V
states.setup: PB4/PB5 set for the 5 V divider tap.
states.source: §5-2 fault code 3305 (band published; the code names no test point)

states.label: Source commanded to 2 V
states.setup: PB4 and PB5 both true, paralleling Z1's 11.535 kohm and 3.846 kohm with its 50 kohm.
states.source: §5-2 fault code 3306 (band published; the code names no test point)

testpoints.condition: During diagnostic 3319: the 2/5/10 V source at 10 V across A10's 1 Mohm string, reading the drop across its 100 kohm portion.
testpoints.note: Published as 1 V ±3 % ±15 mV, which is ±0.030 V + 0.015 V = ±0.045 V. AMP OUT arrives from A10's U1 on P311 pin 30C -- the low-bias-current FET op amp that is switched ahead of A9's U3 for resistances above 1 Mohm (§2-184), which is exactly why the 1 Mohm ratio diagnostic is the one that names this point. The verdict branches: out of tolerance blames A10, in tolerance blames A9.

Output of the differential amplifier, at U4 through R46, on its way to K10 and the RCL line. Nominal gain is 75 (§2-183, fault 3309). The manual publishes no level here because every check of this amplifier is made through A11's adc on RCL rather than at the board: 3308 looks for less than 1 mV spread and less than 10 mV absolute over ten readings with both inputs at 0 V, 3309 for a gain within 6 % of 75 with 86.7 mV on the -input, and 3310 for less than 1 mV of noise. Since every ratio and check code in the 3311-3341 range measures through this amplifier, a fault here lights up nearly the whole block at once -- clear 3304 to 3310 before reading anything into the rest.

testpoints.signal: 2 WIRE COMP. CIRCUIT (1 kohm in Z2, high side)
testpoints.condition: Calibrator at 100 ohm, operate, INT SNS, 2-Wire Comp ON, with a Fluke 8505A on its 100 ohm range across OUTPUT HI and OUTPUT LO sourcing 10 mA.
testpoints.note: The drop across the 1 kohm resistor in Z2, measured DMM hi here and DMM lo on TP6. The manual gives no tolerance -- it says the reading 'should be double and opposite polarity (gain = -2) of that previously measured (about -10V)', the previous measurement being TP18 to TP17. So the real criterion is the ratio to TP18, not this number; the ±20 % band is this dataset's, wide enough not to fail a working board on the manual's own vagueness. U10 senses the current in the high side across the 500 ohm in Z2 and, with Z2's four 10 kohm resistors, drives U9 to push an equal and opposite current through this 1 kohm into the low-side path.

testpoints.signal: 2 WIRE COMP. CIRCUIT (500 ohm in Z2, low side)
testpoints.note: The low end of the 500 ohm resistor in Z2, and the DMM's low lead for the §5-11 step 2 measurement whose hi lead is TP18. It carries no expectation of its own. TP16, TP17 and TP18 all print the same signal name -- '2 WIRE COMP. CIRCUIT' -- in the sheet 1 legend, so the legend alone cannot tell them apart; §5-11 step 2 is what disambiguates them, and the sheet 3 zones do the rest (TP16 at B3, TP17 and TP18 at B5).

testpoints.signal: 2 WIRE COMP. CIRCUIT (500 ohm in Z2, high side)
testpoints.condition: Calibrator at 100 ohm, operate, INT SNS, 2-Wire Comp ON, with a Fluke 8505A on its 100 ohm range across OUTPUT HI and OUTPUT LO sourcing 10 mA.
testpoints.note: The drop across the 500 ohm resistor in Z2, which is the current the ohmmeter is sourcing made visible: 10 mA into 500 ohm is 5 V, which is why the manual says it 'should be around 5.0V'. It publishes no tolerance, so the ±20 % here is this dataset's; take the reading and then check that TP16 is twice it and of opposite polarity. If the 8505A's source current is not really 10 mA this number moves with it, which is why the manual specifies that meter and that range.

The inverting input of the differential amplifier, at U2, fed through K2 from OHMS SENSE HI or through K12 from DAC OUT HI / DAC SENSE HI tied together. No level is published: what the input carries depends entirely on which diagnostic is running. Fault 3309 drives it with 86.7 mV from the DAC to check the gain of 75, and 3308/3310 tie both inputs together through K11 to check offset and noise.

testpoints.condition: During diagnostic 3315: the DAC set to 2 V across the 100 kohm in Z5, reading the divided voltage across its 10 kohm portion.
testpoints.note: The non-inverting input of the differential amplifier, at U3. Fault code 3315 names this point explicitly -- 'verify that the divided DAC voltage of 0.2V ±5% is at the +input of the Diff Amp by connecting DMM hi to TP20 and low to TP10' -- and if it is out of tolerance, A9 is at fault. This is the one check that separates Z5's divider from the rest of the 10 ohm calibration diagnostic. Above 1 Mohm A10's U1 is switched in ahead of U3 (§2-184), so on those ranges this node is driven from AMP OUT rather than from Z5.

probePoints.label: 1 ohm value, four-terminal (TP1/TP2 with sense on TP5/TP6)
probePoints.condition: Calibrator set to 1 ohm, operate, EXT SNS, with a four-terminal ohmmeter such as a Fluke 8505A: IN HI to TP1, IN LO to TP2, SENSE HI to TP5, SENSE LO to TP6.
probePoints.note: The 1 ohm value is four 4 ohm wirewound resistors in parallel inside R41 (§2-175). The measurement is a resistance across a pair of test points rather than a voltage at one, which is why it lives here instead of on TP1. Relays K4 and K5 connect it to OHMS OUT HI and OHMS SENSE HI, K6 and K30 to OHMS OUT LO and OHMS SENSE LO.

probePoints.label: 1.9 ohm value, four-terminal (TP1/TP2 with sense on TP5/TP6)
probePoints.condition: Calibrator set to 1.9 ohm, operate, EXT SNS, same four-terminal connections.
probePoints.note: The 1.9 ohm value is two 3.8 ohm wirewound resistors in parallel inside R42 (§2-175). Note the relay set differs from the 1 ohm case by one: K30 replaces K6.

probePoints.label: Short, four-terminal (TP1/TP2 with sense on TP5/TP6)
probePoints.condition: Calibrator set to 0 ohm, same four-terminal connections.
probePoints.note: Published as '0 ohm ±0.1%', which is not a usable band on a nominal of zero -- 0.1 % of nothing is nothing. The 1 milliohm ceiling here is this dataset's reading of what a four-terminal short check can actually resolve on an 8505A, and it is a ceiling rather than a tolerance for that reason. What the step really asks is whether K7 and K8 are making; a reading in the tens of milliohms or worse is a relay contact, not a calibration error.

probePoints.label: U6 pin 16 (LT3526 switching output)
probePoints.condition: Calibrator at 100 ohm, operate, two-wire comp ON. Scope at 5 V/div, 10 us/div, common on U6 pin 13.
probePoints.note: The only waveform check on this board, and the branch point when both +/-8A rails are wrong. Compare against Figure 5-16. Two things about that figure are worth knowing before you use it: it is captioned 'Waveform at Pin 13 of U6' although the step tells you to probe pin 16 with pin 13 as the common, and its printed axis annotations (1 V, 10 ms) disagree with the scope settings the step gives (5 V/div, 10 us/div). U6 switches +17 S through the T1 primary at about 30 kHz, set by R27 and C21. A wrong waveform sends you to U6, Q5, Q6 and control line PB7; a right one to T1, CR1, CR2, CR9, CR10, VR1 and VR2.

probePoints.label: U7 pins 4 and 5 (chopper amplifier input, differential)
probePoints.condition: Calibrator at 100 ohm, operate, INT SNS, 2-Wire Comp ON, with a Fluke 8505A on its 100 ohm range across OUTPUT HI and OUTPUT LO sourcing 10 mA.
probePoints.note: Published as 'less than 4 uV'. Neither lead goes to a board common -- this is a differential measurement between two pins of the same package, and it is the direct test of whether the high-side cancellation is working: U7 drives U8 so as to hold its own input difference at zero, which forces the voltage drop in the high side path to zero. Recorded in microvolts because that is the range you would use. A failure sends you to U7 and U8.
